To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the treatment with centrophenoxine or a new drug BCE 001 increased the average lateral diffusion coefficient (D) of membrane proteins of the hepatocyte plasma membranes of old rats.
the lateral diffusion of membrane proteins is decreased in aging and can be increased by drugs that have antioxidant properties.
the age-dependent loss of body weight of old rats can be prevented by treatment with the new drug BCE 001, which also increases the lateral diffusion of membrane proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method for measuring the lateral diffusion of membrane proteins, and with the in vivo evaluation of the effects of drugs on the age dependent loss and recovery of this parameter.
the effects of two drugs, centrophenoxine CPH and BCE-001, on the lateral diffusion of proteins of the plasma membrane of rat liver cells.
the effects of two drugs, centrophenoxine CPH) and a new drug, BCE 001, on the lateral diffusion coefficient of membrane proteins in the hepatocytes of young and old male rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drug effects on membrane fluidity and the consequent improvement of membrane and cellular function are a consequence of the drug effects on the OH. free radical level.

the drugs tested have the ability to retard the rate of loss of body weight and to increase the lateral diffusion of proteins of the hepatocyte plasma membranes of old animals, but they are not able to prevent the age related decrease of the latter parameter in the young animals.
the two drugs tested have an age dependent beneficial effect on the membrane function in the liver cells of old rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the age dependent increase of the membrane rigidity is due to the accumulation in the cell membrane proteins of oxidized flavin residues which are responsible for a decrease in the average lateral diffusion coefficient D of the membrane proteins.
the age related decrease of membrane D is a marker of aging, which may be reversed by drugs acting on the membrane.

a decrease of the average diffusion coefficient of proteins in the membrane of hepatocytes is a reliable index of the age dependent loss in the quality of the membrane and that a proper treatment with OH. free radical trapping agents is capable of restoring the normal value of this parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FRAP technique can be used to monitor the effect of a variety of drugs on the plasma membrane of hepatocytes.
the use of the PIAF method in liver smears is a reliable tool for the evaluation of membrane function.

a new drug, BCE 001, which is able to retard the aging process in rats and which is also able to restore the lateral diffusion of proteins of the cell membrane to normal values, may have a potential for use as an anti-aging drug.
